references.text: Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit when he returned from the Jordan – this verse shows the same power of the Spirit that now drives him back to Galilee.
At Jesus' baptism, the Holy Spirit came down upon him. The power of the Spirit mentioned in 4:14 has its origin in this event.
Matthew's parallel account of Jesus returning to Galilee after the temptation in the wilderness.
Mark's parallel account of Jesus coming to Galilee and proclaiming the gospel of God.
John also tells of Jesus' arrival in Galilee and how the Galileans received him, which aligns with the rumor about him spreading.
Peter summarizes Jesus' ministry that began in Galilee, and how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and power – a direct parallel to the power of the Spirit mentioned in Luke 4:14.
Even as a child, Jesus grew in favor with God and people, and now the rumor about him spreads throughout the entire region.
The rumor about Jesus spread to all places in the surrounding area – a repetition of the theme from verse 14 regarding his growing reputation.

Isaiah's prophecy about the Lord's Spirit being upon the anointed one – this is the messianic text that Jesus himself reads aloud shortly afterward in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:18), and the power of the Spirit in verse 14 is the fulfillment of this prophecy.
Matthew describes similarly how the rumor about Jesus spread throughout all Syria, and large crowds followed him, paralleling the report that went out over the entire region in Luke 4:14.
Paul speaks of signs and wonders in the power of the Holy Spirit – the same expression 'power of the Spirit' (δύναμις τοῦ πνεύματος) is used here as in Luke 4:14.
